pr_title: Fix shadow peter-panning with default spotlight
pr_body:
Fixes #101857.

A regression with default spotlights exhibiting significant shadow peter-panning was introduced in #100319.

This PR fixes it with 2 changes :
1. sets the now-fixed light znear to *0.025* instead of *0.005*. This is to match the former behavior of default spotlights and omnis (*range = 5* driving *znear = 0.005 * 5 = 0.025*)
2. applies bias as a constant offset in clip space. Now znear is fixed, *z = w* in clip space always represents the same *z = znear* in view space, therefore there is no need to rescale bias before applying it in clip space anymore

This is how default point lights' shadows look like with this PR.
Appearance also does not depend on range.
| Default Spotlight | Default Omni |
| --- | --- |
| range = 5 and bias =  0.03| range = 5 and bias = 0.1 |
| ![Capture d’écran du 2025-01-23 09-19-01](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73a6d7d0-d504-4caa-9739-cb7d213c84d8) | ![Capture d’écran du 2025-01-23 09-19-34](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a99580f5-de46-4cf1-91e4-13ae7357f862) |

I'd need other pairs of eyes especially on change no. 2. I was originally counting on Omni shadows implementation to serve as a reference to double check Spotlight implementation, but it turned out that they are rather different both code-wise and math-wise.
pr_comments:
> while shadowing does work correctly initially, it will break down once you change the spot range again

This is weird. I've no clue right now. I've been playing with large range lights but didn't notice that yet.

Also, is the stripped pattern on both your captures an issue with self shadowing ? Does increasing the bias solve it ? 

The whole purpose of the original PR #100319 is to allow large range lights so I'd be concerned if it's still broken out of the box 😅

@Calinou I watched your videos very closely again.

I don't have the impression the building's shadows change before / after you reset the light´s range.

See these captures from the 1st video : 
| Before re-changing | After re-changing |
|---|---|
|![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5863eb34-2a3e-4552-81fd-41e98b047e93)|![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/783a6d02-b044-4a0a-a7a4-900c27b962bd)|

What's changing for sure is the stripped pattern exhibited by the spotlight that I cannot understand right now unless it's self shadowing.

@Calinou, are you using 4,4,16,64 quadrants? to me it seems like what happened is a quadrant shift, which is a bit buggy

If that is the case Retest with all quadrants at the same value (4,4,4,4 or 16,16,16,16 or 64,64,64,64)

> @Calinou, are you using 4,4,16,64 quadrants? to me it seems like what happened is a quadrant shift, which is a bit buggy

I was using the default quadrant project settings. The project has a fair amount of shadow-casting spotlights (more than 8), so maybe it was due to that.

This had been bugging me since 4.4-dev7. Happy to see it fixed!

| Before  | After |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03211bb5-6b49-4a1b-8a2b-aae3d6a84258)  | ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22ce1efb-963d-416a-9652-2353db55cc63)  |

I made tests with the MRP provided by @Calinou.

### Banding artifacts
The banding is self-shadowing artifacts.
Increasing the bias a little bit gets rid of them, at the cost of loosing shadows on smaller details.
I believe there is nothing wrong in this, just the normal behavior when the light's range gets bigger and the geometry farther away.

The only point still unclear is why such banding doesn't appear with an Omni light instead of a Spotlight, with identical settings. I think it's related to the resolution of the shadow map (spotlights have a single texture where omnis have a cubemap), but this assumption would deserve to be confirmed.

### Possibly broken shadowing when changing range

> while shadowing does work correctly initially, it will break down once you change the spot range again

I couldn't reproduce that. And I couldn't see anything going wrong with the shadows in any of the 2 videos you shared (see my previous comment https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/101952#issuecomment-2613841780)

What I noticed though in the MRP is that there is no banding artifact at startup. They re-appeared as soon as I changed the light's range. It's like the bias was set internally to a high value (no self-shadowing) and got back to normal then.

Worth also noting that after saving the project with another very large range and repoening it, I couldn't reproduce this anymore. So it's still not clear what's the cause of if, but I think it's unrelated to this PR.

> Worst case scenario we get more regressions in beta 3 and then we can just revert for 4.4 and try again for 4.5

Agree. For later reference in case we need to move back, we'll need to revert all three #100319, #100862 and this one. This will revert spotlight shadows to the exact 4.3 behavior.

issue_context.title: SpotLight3D shadow has significant peter-panning with default settings (4.4-dev7 and 4.4-beta1)
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.4-dev7 and 4.4-beta1
Not reproducible in: 4.4-dev6 and before

### System information

Godot v4.4.dev7 - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Single-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6603) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 threads)

### Issue description

Shadow casting SpotLight3D has noticeable peter-panning effect with default bias value. Example below:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/501f57ff-6c38-477d-aa8e-0e2e695ab5ba)

### Steps to reproduce

Create a new 3D scene
Add floor into the scene and add mesh on the floor
Add SpotLight3D and enable shadows
Point the spotlight towards mesh and observe shadow it casts

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
comments:
Bisected to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100319, CC @Flarkk

It doesn't seem like this was an intentional or expected change, can confirm this with a very normal setup, see MRP

[MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18494408/MRP.zip)

What's the bias of the spotlight in the MRP ? 0.1 or 0.001 ? (I don't have my computer at hand right now).

I remember there was a hard coded factor somewhere for spotlights bias I had trouble with until I figured it out at the time of writing #100319
It's default settings, which should be sufficient in this case I'd say, everything is bog standard

I'm wondering whether the standard value could have changed and make this issue apparent now but not at the time of my PR. 

This is because I remember that at this time the bias input was multiplied or divided by 100 or something for spotlights somewhere before being passed to the rendering logic (don't know why). If this has changed since then it can have a material impact.

Will check when I get back to my computer.

But if the default value changed it wouldn't show up, because the default isn't stored, so a project created in 4.4.beta1 would still show up the same at the time the PR was merged, it *could* have changed while you were working on it though, but it was apparent at the time of merger

It occurs immediately at the PR, and at the merged branch (i.e. without rebase), but not immediately before it

Oh yes it's not stored, you're right.
Will take a look.

I found that the problem is the 0.005 I chose for the fixed light znear, thinking that the default light range was 1 and that this would behave like before (znear = 0.005 * range).

But the default range is actually 5, so znar has to be 0.025 to behave as before with the default setup.

With that fixed I noticed something else : peter-panning now visibly grows with the spotlight's range even at reasonable values. This is not the case with Omnis that now behave exactly like before.

I'm now investigating whether it could be related to the hardcoded bias factor set to spotlights I mentioned above :
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a7146ef807a7676f51a8a63cf4441ad647f4be66/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/light_storage.cpp#L963-L967

Will issue a PR once I resolved this too.

Done. Anyone please test #101952 extensively with both Omnis and Spotlights, default and non default ranges, bias, positions, shadow modes and other settings.

Changes are rather simple but it's the second regression I'm fixing related to my original PR #100319 so it makes me think it's bug prone code.

review_comments: This will work at the default radius, but its going to break once the radius changes isn't it?

It works with all radiuses, and it's not related to the value of the constant (this adjustment is only meant to align the new default behavior with the previous one).

The reason why it works irrespective of the range is different for Omnis and Spotlights : 

#### For Omnis
Bias is applied in **view space** as a constant  z-offset :
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d08ff57148c42b63e74adb669f6937d35fde1f6e/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl#L435-L437
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d08ff57148c42b63e74adb669f6937d35fde1f6e/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl#L543

This is because `omni_lights.data[idx].shadow_matrix` is **not a projection matrix** as its name may suggest but [the light's modelview matrix](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d08ff57148c42b63e74adb669f6937d35fde1f6e/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/light_storage.cpp#L982-L984).

:point_right: None of the above depend on the shadow *projection* matrix, therefore the bias does not depend on the range.

#### For Spotlights
Bias is applied in **clip space**, now as a constant z-offset (see diff of scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl).

This is because unlike Omnis, `spot_lights.data[idx].shadow_matrix` *is* the [shadow projection matrix](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d08ff57148c42b63e74adb669f6937d35fde1f6e/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/light_storage.cpp#L1004-L1006).

But because znear is a small constant since #100319, clip space z coordinate does not depend on znear, nor on zfar as long as it is significantly larger than znear (consequence of `proj[2][2] = -(f+n)/(f-n)` converging to -1 when `n` is small). And if any use case would require the light range to be as low as 0.025 and shadows are on, visual artifacts would be very very small.

:point_right: the bias is constant irrespective of the range.

Makes sense. I'm still a bit skeptical, but at least now the behaviour for lights at and smaller than the default range is the same as it was in 4.3. 

As Calinou highlights, this change maintains the high risk of self-shadowing for high ranges (since there will be a noticeable precision loss when increasing the range much higher than the default

Happy to clarify or do anything more to make you fully comfortable with it.

> this change maintains the high risk of self-shadowing for high ranges

Self shadowing happens with large ranges *only on far away geometry* : now we use reverse-z precision is much less of a problem even with very small z-near.

This means there should not be any visual change with shadows on reasonably closeby geometry, even with large light ranges.
